manifest.name: App Builder
manifest.description: vibe app authoring tool — 8-layer model (App / Theme / Component / Dashboard / Navigation / Page / Assets / Whole) + Live Reactive Preview + Dart / Embed converters. Chat with the manager to scaffold, design, and convert new app projects. Migrated from vibe_app_builder (AUTHOR scope only — host surfaces absorbed into vibe_studio builtins).

agents.name: App Builder Manager
agents.systemPrompt: You are the manager agent for App Builder — an mcp_ui_dsl app authoring surface inside vibe_studio. Classify the user's intent and dispatch: (a) NEW APP → studio.project.new + studio.workspace.adopt (use the newAppProject tool); (b) EDIT 8-LAYER → ux_designer for wireframes, ui_implementer for mcp_ui_dsl JSON via studio.builder.* mutators; (c) CONVERT → dart_converter for `.app` standalone, embed_converter for LVGL / Qt firmware; (d) PREVIEW → studio.chrome.reload_tab to refresh the VbuPreviewMcpUi; (e) KNOWLEDGE QUERY → studio.knowledge.query under sourceId='app_builder_six_layers' / 'app_builder_wiring' / 'app_builder_pitfalls' / 'dart_conversion_patterns' / 'embed_conversion_patterns'. Authoring uses the studio.builder.* mutators only (no studio.fs.write of canonical paths). When a needed mutator is missing, stop and surface 'host defect — needs <mutator>' so the user can approve a host fix.

agents.name: UX Designer
agents.systemPrompt: You design wireframes for one of the 8 layers (App · Theme · Component · Dashboard · Navigation · Page · Assets · Whole). Inputs: blueprint or user request. Output (markdown): (1) PURPOSE — one line. (2) WIDGETS — list of vbu_* atoms + their props (label, icon, state binding). (3) LAYOUT — text sketch (linear · box · expanded · sized). (4) WIRING — which buttons dispatch which tools (camelCase, named after manifest.tools[].name). (5) STATE BINDINGS — `{{key}}` references and where they live in state.initial. Query studio.knowledge.query under sourceId='app_builder_wiring' for action shape conventions before writing.

agents.name: Tool Designer
agents.systemPrompt: Given a wireframe + verb list from ux_designer, design the kind:'js' tools that drive the dynamic behaviour. For each: name (camelCase verb), inputSchema (JSON Schema), outputSchema (top-level keys named to match state keys for auto-merge per mcp_ui_dsl spec §3.10), and JS source body. Body conventions: receive `args` (current state slice) + global `host` (host.fs / host.kb / host.mcp / host.ui / host.workspace / host.bundle); return JSON-serializable object whose keys map to state. Add tools via studio.builder.addTool. Query studio.knowledge.query under sourceId='app_builder_six_layers' + 'app_builder_pitfalls' for tool boundaries.

agents.name: Knowledge Designer
agents.systemPrompt: Design the 6-category cold-start knowledge for a new app project (sources · facts · skills · profiles · philosophies · workflows). For App Builder itself the seeded sources are app_builder_six_layers / app_builder_wiring / app_builder_pitfalls / dart_conversion_patterns / embed_conversion_patterns. Add new sources / docs via studio.builder.addKnowledgeSource + addKnowledgeDoc. Each doc is plain markdown — query existing knowledge first to avoid duplication.

agents.name: UI Implementer
agents.systemPrompt: Materialise the wireframe + tool list into mcp_ui_dsl 1.3 JSON. Lowercase canonical widget names (page / box / linear / text / button / list / sizedBox / card / conditional / switch / expanded / icon). PascalCase for custom widgets (Vbu* / Tool*). Bind click handlers as `click:{type:'tool', tool:'<exposedName>', params:{...}}` — NEVER `action:`. State binding via `state.initial` + `{{key}}` templates. Page lifecycle uses `lifecycle.onInit` (mcp_ui_dsl 1.3 hook) for first-mount data load — action shape `{type:'tool', name:'<tool>'}`. Application root = `type:'application'` envelope with initialRoute + routes; pages live at `ui/pages/<id>.json`. After writing call studio.chrome.reload_tab so the change surfaces.

agents.name: Dart Converter
agents.systemPrompt: Convert the canonical .mbd (manifest + ui + tools + knowledge) into a self-contained Flutter Dart project written under `build/dart/` of the active app project. Output structure: pubspec.yaml · lib/main.dart (bootstraps MCPUIRuntime with the bundle embedded as Dart maps) · assets/ (copied from app.mbd/assets) · README.md. Generate the Dart code as a single LLM call (no hand-written templates per [[feedback_vibe_codegen_is_llm]]). Write via studio.fs.write through host.fs atom. After write, return `{ok:true, path:'<build/dart>'}`.

agents.name: Embed Converter
agents.systemPrompt: Convert the canonical mcp_ui_dsl into LVGL (C) or Qt (C++) source under `build/embed/<flavor>/`. Read the spec from knowledge corpus before generating — embedded targets have strict memory / no-alloc constraints documented under sourceId='embed_conversion_patterns'. Default flavor=LVGL. Output: src/ui_<page>.c · src/ui_main.c · CMakeLists.txt · README.md. Generate via LLM call (no hand-written code templates).

agents.name: Debug Analyst
agents.systemPrompt: You are the debug specialist for the unified builder. Your domain is the Debug mode (inspector / runtime state / dispatch log / variant cards / scenario replay). Tools you typically use: studio.debug.runtime_state, studio.debug.dispatch_log, studio.debug.layout_snapshot, studio.debug.screenshot, studio.debug.activation, studio.scenario.* (when present), studio.recorder.* (when present). Read the wire log + state snapshot to localise an issue, then propose the smallest reproduction + concrete fix path. Do not mutate the bundle's manifest — that is the bundle / authoring specialists' job.

sources.title: App Builder — 8-Layer Model
sources.description: Canonical 8-layer authoring model (App · Theme · Component · Dashboard · Navigation · Page · Assets · Whole) — what each layer owns and which manifest section it maps to. NOTE: these layers are an App Builder INTERNAL authoring abstraction, not bundle manifest sections. The bundle spec defines no manifest.theme / manifest.templates / manifest.dashboard / manifest.navigation — that data lives in ui/app.json (mcp_ui_dsl ApplicationDefinition) + mcp_ui_dsl templates.

documents.title: Layer 01 — App
documents.content: App layer owns bundle metadata: `manifest.manifest.{id, name, version, description}`, `schemaVersion`, top-level `type`. Identity + packaging. UI placeholder shows id + name + description with edit affordances. Save = studio.builder.patchManifest({patch:{manifest:{...}}}).

documents.title: Layer 02 — Theme
documents.content: Theme layer (App Builder INTERNAL model — NOT a bundle manifest section) = the M3 theme tokens declared inside ui/app.json under the mcp_ui_dsl ApplicationDefinition `theme` (e.g. theme.typography, color tokens) — there is no manifest.theme section in the bundle spec. Token shape: colorScheme.{primary, secondary, tertiary, surface, surface1..5, error, onPrimary, ...}. UI shows color swatch grid + brightness toggle (light/dark/auto) + font picker. App Builder persists edits by writing ui/app.json (studio.builder.writeUI) — patchManifest is for top-level manifest fields, not theme.

documents.title: Layer 03 — Component
documents.content: Component layer (App Builder INTERNAL model — NOT a bundle manifest section) = reusable widget templates per the mcp_ui_dsl spec §template. There is no manifest.templates section in the bundle spec — templates are authored inside the UI definition (ui/app.json + ui/ page files). Each template = {id, parameters:[{key,type,default}], body:<widget tree>}; instantiate with the `use` widget. UI shows template list + per-template editor. Save via studio.builder.lib.create / .placeInline / .read / .rename.

documents.title: Layer 04 — Dashboard
documents.content: Dashboard layer (App Builder INTERNAL model — NOT a bundle manifest section) = a metric / dashboard page authored as an mcp_ui_dsl PageDefinition (card + label + value/chart widgets) inside ui/. There is no manifest.dashboard section in the bundle spec. State binding pulls live data through page state bindings or `data:` URIs. Save by writing the page under ui/ (studio.builder.writeUI / ui.applyPatch) — not patchManifest.

documents.title: Layer 05 — Navigation
documents.content: Navigation layer (App Builder INTERNAL model — NOT a bundle manifest section) = the route map + navigation chrome declared inside ui/app.json under the mcp_ui_dsl ApplicationDefinition (`routes` map of path -> PageDefinition / "ui://" URI, plus `navigation.type` drawer/bottomBar/rail/tabs + `navigation.items`). There is no manifest.navigation section in the bundle spec. Save by writing ui/app.json (studio.builder.writeUI / ui.applyPatch) — not patchManifest.

documents.title: Layer 06 — Page
documents.content: Page layer = `ui/pages/<id>.json` files. Each page = {type:'page', title, content:<widget tree>, state:{initial:{...}}, lifecycle:{onInit:[...]}}. New page = studio.builder.ui.applyPatch on routes + writeUI to create the file. State.initial declares all state keys the page reads; values without initial entry default to empty string. lifecycle.onInit fires on first mount + on resume.

documents.title: Layer 07 — Assets
documents.content: Assets layer = `manifest.assets` (images / fonts / icons) under `app.mbd/assets/`. Reference via `asset:<id>` or `assets/<path>` URI from widgets (icon, image). Save = studio.fs.write under app.mbd/assets/ + studio.builder.patchManifest to register the entry.

documents.title: Layer 08 — Whole
documents.content: Whole layer = composite view of the application — envelope (type:'application' + initialRoute + routes) + page bag + service map + theme + manifest summary. Read-only consolidated view; mutations land on the individual layers, this view re-derives.

sources.title: App Builder — Wiring conventions
sources.description: How buttons, slash commands, lifecycle slots, and domain icons are wired across an mcp_ui_dsl bundle. Mirrors the in-bundle wiring section.

documents.title: Action shape — click handlers
documents.content: Canonical click handler shape: `{"type":"tool", "tool":"<exposedName>", "params":{...}}`. NEVER use `"action":...`. The runtime IGNORES `action`. Optional `onSuccess` / `onError` for chained actions. Tool name = manifest.tools[].name (camelCase verb) — no shortId prefix in the bundle's own tools.

documents.title: Page lifecycle — onInit/onMount
documents.content: mcp_ui_dsl 1.3 page-level hooks: onInit (first mount, before paint), onReady (after first frame), onMount (after attach to navigator), onPause / onResume (visibility), onUnmount / onDestroy (teardown). Action list shape: `[{type:'tool', name:'<tool>'}, ...]`. For first-mount data loads (e.g. studio.scenario.list), put the tool call in `onInit`. Application-level lifecycle is also `onInit`.

documents.title: manifest.wiring.domainActions[]
documents.content: Row 2 of ProjectHeader renders each entry. Two kinds: `button` (single icon + tooltip + onTap) and `selectGroup` (stateKey-driven row of items with emphasis when matching value). selectGroup item: {icon, tooltip, value, tool, args} — on tap dispatches tool then sets state[stateKey]=value. App Builder's 8-card strip is a selectGroup with stateKey='focused' and 8 items (appStructure, theme, components, dashboard, navigation, pages, assets, whole).

documents.title: manifest.wiring.lifecycle[]
documents.content: Row 1 system buttons of ProjectHeader. 9 canonical slots: project.new, project.open, project.save, edit.undo, edit.redo, history.show, edit.revert, project.close, project.export. Each entry: {slot, tool, args?}. Unbound slot = button disabled. App Builder binds project.new → newAppProject tool, project.save → studio.builder.patchManifest noop (writes are immediate), project.export → convertToDart with default flavor.

documents.title: manifest.chat.slashCommands[]
documents.content: Slash chips above the chat composer. Each entry: {command:'/<name>', description, directDispatch?:{tool, args}}. directDispatch fires the tool immediately on chip tap (skipping the manager); without it the slash text expands into the input. App Builder seeds 6: /new (→ newAppProject), /convert (→ manager classify), /preview (→ studio.chrome.reload_tab), /install (→ studio.bundle.install picker), /find (→ studio.knowledge.query), /embed (→ convertToEmbed).

documents.title: manifest.wiring.titlebar / wiring.statusbar — chrome user zones (spec §6.4a)
documents.content: Two optional single-string fields on the wiring section that render in the studio host's chrome user areas. `wiring.titlebar`: rendered in the titlebar between the fixed pills (server URL · transport · version) and the right edge. `wiring.statusbar`: rendered in the statusbar between the host's fixed lint group and the right edge (version · locale). Both support `{{key}}` bindings against the active tab's runtime state (dot paths like `{{foo.bar}}` walk maps; missing keys interpolate to empty string). Host enforces ONE single payload — do not try to declare items[]. If the bundle needs multiple pieces, combine them in a tool / state binding and emit one string. The host clears both zones on Home / inactive tabs (no last-write-wins leak). Schema: `"wiring": {"titlebar": "build {{status}} · {{commit}}", "statusbar": "recordings: {{count}}"}`. Edit path: BundleManifestView's CHROME ZONES section (300ms debounce autosave; empty value removes the key). Round-trip preserve since mcp_bundle 0.3.3 (WiringSection.titlebar / statusbar String? fields). Use this for live state surfacing (build status, count, last activity) — NOT for static branding (that goes in manifest.name / icon).

sources.title: App Builder — Common pitfalls
sources.description: Recurring mistakes inherited from vibe_app_builder (28k LOC source). Read before authoring.

documents.title: Raw box/linear/text/button hand-roll
documents.content: Never hand-roll page chrome with raw `box`/`linear`/`text`/`button` when a Vbu* atom exists. The atoms ship the host-vetted tone (mono / mint / surface3) and survive theme changes; raw widgets drift. Use VbuTitleBar / VbuPaneHeader / VbuFormSection / VbuLabelled* / VbuTabStrip / VbuRouter / VbuDomainActionsRow / VbuPathTile / VbuPill — full catalog in studio-widget-catalog.md. Raw widgets only at leaf level inside an atom.

documents.title: `action:` vs `click:` confusion
documents.content: Runtime accepts `click:` (button + tappable) and `onTap:` (alias). `action:` is silently IGNORED. If a button shows but does nothing on tap, check for `action:` instead of `click:` — most common dead-button cause.

documents.title: State keys without state.initial
documents.content: Every state key referenced via `{{key}}` MUST appear in state.initial. Otherwise the template binds to empty string and the conditional / switch branches surprisingly. Add `key: <default>` to state.initial when introducing a new binding.

documents.title: VbuPreviewMcpUi target binding
documents.content: VbuPreviewMcpUi.bundlePath must point to the user's app project (not App Builder's own bundle). Bind `{{currentProject}}` via state.initial + manager's newAppProject tool which writes currentProject after scaffold. Empty currentProject = the preview shows 'No bundle to embed yet' placeholder (canonical inert wireframe; do not fallback to self-mount).

documents.title: Converter codegen via LLM
documents.content: Dart / Embed converter outputs are LLM-generated (per [[feedback_vibe_codegen_is_llm]]). Never embed hand-written code templates in the converter JS — the JS just orchestrates the LLM call (host.mcp.dispatch to dart_converter agent), writes the LLM result to disk via host.fs.write, and returns the build path.

documents.title: Bundle artifact purity — never write non-content inside the bundle
documents.content: A .mbd/.mcpb directory must contain ONLY distributable bundle content (manifest.json, ui/, knowledge/, tools/, scenarios/, assets/ — spec sections). NEVER write authoring byproducts or runtime state (history snapshots, undo data, caches, registries, conversation logs, temp files, dot-files) inside the bundle directory: everything inside the artifact ships with it — packers, uploads, and resource resolvers all treat it as bundle content. Real incident (2026-07-13): in-bundle .history snapshots got packed and a marketplace serving shell served a STALE page copy over the live one. Where things go instead: mutation history = the sibling root `<parent>/.history-<bundleDirName>/` (bundle_history.dart); project/workspace state = the project root, never the bundle. Content writes go through the bundle layer only (studio.builder.* mutators / the bundle writer) — no raw file writes into the artifact from arbitrary code. This applies equally when you author bundle apps: never design a bundle that stores its own runtime state inside its .mbd.

sources.title: App Builder — app/bundle design methodology
sources.description: How to DESIGN and BUILD a real app or domain package on App Builder end to end (the optimal decision flow), tying the per-topic sources (8-layer, wiring, pitfalls, dart/embed, ux/ops/knowledge patterns, external-LLM) into one order. Use this to coach the user from a blank project to a packed/installed bundle. Canonical human handbook: docs/app_builder/APP-DESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md.

documents.title: Build philosophy & decision flow
documents.content:
# Building an app/bundle on App Builder

The output unit is a BUNDLE (.mbd -> packed .mcpb): either an appPlayerApp (a declarative mcp_ui_dsl 1.3 app AppPlayer renders) or a studioPackage (a domain package that runs inside the studio). Four principles frame every decision:
- declarative-first: the app is a canonical mcp_ui_dsl JSON tree (widgets/state/actions/theme as data), not hand-written Flutter. That's why an LLM can author/validate/convert it.
- atom-first: start from canonical widgets + Vbu custom widgets (ToolForm, VbuTitleBar, ...), not hand-rolled box/linear/text/button. Hand-rolling is almost always an anti-pattern.
- patch-only: every edit is a CanonicalPatch (RFC 6902) -> dry-run validate -> atomic apply (or ValidationReport). This gives deterministic undo/redo and .history/ snapshots. Don't bypass by hand-writing files.
- verify-as-gate: lenient while authoring (fast iteration), strict at activation (schema + cross-ref + hash). Pass lint/a11y/validate/grade/checkWiring at each step.

Decision flow: (1) decide kind + output target -> (2) build the 8 layers top-down -> (3) lay out UI from atoms -> (4) attach state + wiring -> (5) (package) add tools/knowledge/agents -> (6) pass verification gates -> (7) convert/pack/distribute.

documents.title: Kind, output target, and the 8 layers
documents.content:
# Pick the kind + target, then model 8 layers top-down

ProjectKind (first decision, no conversion between kinds):
- appPlayerApp -> user-facing app (POS/LMS/report); preview = PreviewMcpUi (pure mcp_ui_dsl).
- studioPackage -> domain package with tools/knowledge/agents; preview = DslWorkspaceView variant (vbu_* atoms).

Output target (sets depth/conversion): AppPlayer bundle (.mbd/.mcpb, fully supported) · studio domain package (bundle.install, internal-gated) · Dart (5 variants, SCAFFOLD + insertion markers, NOT full transpile) · embedded C/LVGL (placeholder scaffold only) · self-UI. AppPlayer app and domain package are the first-class complete paths; Dart/embedded are generative scaffolds the user/LLM fills in.

8-layer UI model, build TOP-DOWN (each layer constrains the next): appStructure (name/route/nav style) -> theme (color/typography/spacing TOKENS first, so widgets reference tokens not hardcodes) -> component (reusable templates) -> dashboard -> navigation -> page (most authoring happens here) -> assets -> whole (full canonical JSON, expert). Bundle mode has 4 layers (manifest/tools/knowledge/agents) = the package's identity. Multi-language/variant = CHANNELS (serving/native/custom; create/activate/diff/swap), not duplicated pages.

documents.title: UI authoring, state & wiring
documents.content:
# Lay out from atoms; attach state + wiring correctly

UI: start from the canonical page shape (header/body/footer) and the 154-widget catalog + Vbu custom widgets (desktop TOOL aesthetic, not mobile). Three authoring paths, all through the same patch pipeline: chat ('add a button' -> manager patches), catalog drag, MCP-direct (external LLM calls build.add_child/setProperty = driving mode). Keep the tree clean with treeOutline/widgetShapeAudit/widgetLint/tokenizationAudit/routeAudit before pages grow.

State + wiring is where most pitfalls live — exact shapes matter:
- every state key MUST be declared in state.initial (else bindings break).
- bindings are {{path}}; equality/arithmetic bindings are NOT supported (compute via tools/state).
- tool action shape is {type:'tool', tool:'<name>', params:{...}} (NOT action+args).
- a button's handler is the click property (NOT action).
- lifecycle.onInit auto-loads on mount; tool responses auto-merge into state (spec 3.10) so design the response shape to match the state shape.
- surface every tool to the user via manifest.wiring.domainActions / wiring.settings / chat.slashCommands, so nothing is 'present but uncallable'.
Order: sketch the state shape -> match tool responses to it -> onInit to initialize -> click/action to mutate -> wiring to surface.

documents.title: Package: tools, knowledge, agents
documents.content:
# For a studioPackage: capabilities, knowledge, agents

Tools (the package's capability): kind:js writes tools/<name>.js + manifest.tools.tools[] (addTool); kind=mcp (external http/stdio server) and wasm also supported. Declare requires.builtinAtoms (mcp/fs/workspace/ui/browser/form/io/kv/db/secret...) so capabilities are injected at boot — DON'T reimplement host capabilities (browser/form/io...), pull them via requires. Domain storage = host.kb.put/get/list/delete (KV) + host.kb.query (knowledge search); don't invent a store.

Knowledge (6 categories, see knowledge_design_patterns): chunks(sources[].documents) · facts(SVO) · skills · profiles · philosophies · agents. Cold-start minimum = an overview chunk + key facts + one manager agent. Use addKnowledgeSource/addKnowledgeDoc/addSkill/addProfile/addPhilosophy/addFact/addAgent.

Agents: a manager + specialists pattern (the App Builder seed itself ships manager + ux_designer/ui_implementer/tool_designer/knowledge_designer/dart_converter/embed_converter/debug_analyst). The manager classifies intent and delegates via bk.agent.dispatch({agentId}). Design the package's own pool the same way. (Note: in the debug build, FlowBrain orchestration is only partially activated — design delegation, but verify execution in an activated environment.)

documents.title: Verify, convert, and checklist
documents.content:
# Gates, conversion, and a design checklist

Verification gates (lenient while authoring, strict at activation): build.lint/lintCanonical · build.a11y_audit · build.validate/validateBundle · checkWiring (routes/component refs/action bindings) · build.grade (composite) · build.design_critique. Preview: PreviewMcpUi (appPlayerApp) vs DslWorkspaceView variant (studioPackage), with previewCapture (PNG) + layoutSnapshot (real rects without a vision model). External-LLM authoring follows the external_llm_app_builder lockdown (stage flow A->G, 12 lockdown points, self-verification gate, permission boundary).

Convert/pack/distribute: pack_bundle -> .mcpb; domain install via bundle.install (INTERNAL-gated, no external-LLM call); distribute the .mcpb. Honest limits: Dart conversion = scaffold + insertion markers (no full widget->Dart transpile); embedded C/LVGL = placeholder scaffold (no LVGL binding/HAL); i18n = locale management only; layout presets are fixed. Don't design as if Dart/embedded auto-generate full logic.

Checklist: kind + output target chosen first? 8 layers top-down (theme tokens before pages)? started from atoms/Vbu, not hand-rolled? state.initial declared, action=type/params, button=click? tool response shape matches state shape (auto-merge)? every tool surfaced via wiring? package declares requires.builtinAtoms + uses host.kb? passed lint/a11y/validate/grade/checkWiring at each step? multi-language via channels, not page copies? not mistaking Dart/embedded scaffolds for full auto-conversion?

documents.title: Output layout
documents.content:
build/embed/lvgl/<name>/
  src/ui_main.c           — ui_init() builds the screen tree, ui_event_<page>() handlers per page
  src/ui_<page>.c         — per-page builders
  inc/ui.h                — public ui_init prototype
  CMakeLists.txt          — list .c sources, link lvgl
  README.md               — integration: include lv_conf.h, call ui_init() after lv_init()

documents.title: Memory + no-alloc constraints
documents.content: Embedded targets cannot allocate during a frame. All lv_obj* are created in ui_init() and reused (visibility / text / src updated via setters). State bindings cannot use string templating at runtime — compile templates to setter call sequences in ui_<page>.c. Lifecycle.onInit calls become explicit init function calls inside ui_init().

sources.name: Embed Conversion Patterns

documents.title: accessibleWrapper widget
documents.content:
`accessibleWrapper` — utility, Core profile. Wraps a child with accessibility annotations (ARIA-style). See [`13_Accessibility.md`](13_Accessibility.md) for the full property set.
Required: child:Widget.
Optional: accessibility:object, announceNavigation:boolean, announceOnChange:boolean, autoFocus:boolean, focusGroup:string, focusOrder:number, liveRegion:string (one of polite|assertive|status|alert), navigationMessage:string, watchPath:string.

documents.title: accordion widget
documents.content:
`accordion` (also `collapsible`) — layout, Core profile. Sections that expand and collapse. `children` are the panels; each panel declares its own `title` (or a `header` widget) and body. Composing this from `conditional` + `inkWell` renders correctly and loses two things the author cannot add back: the expand/collapse transition, and the accessibility state a screen reader announces (expanded / collapsed, and which control owns which region). A collapsed section that is merely absent from the tree reads to assistive technology as content that does not exist rather than content that is hidden. `collapsible` is an alias for the single-section case — one panel with `allowMultiple` irrelevant. It is the same widget, not a smaller one.
Required: panels:array<object>.
Optional: allowMultiple:boolean (default false), bordered:boolean (default true), expandedIds:array<string>, icon:IconRef.

documents.title: alertDialog widget
documents.content:
`alertDialog` (also `alert`, `confirmDialog`) — dialog, Core profile. Modal alert with an optional title, an optional body (string or widget), and a list of labeled action buttons. Dispatched via the `dialog` action (`{ "type": "dialog", "dialog": { "type": "alertDialog", ... } }`). The runtime renders it as a `Dialog` surface scoped to the current navigator (not the root navigator), so tapping an action pops only the dialog.
Optional: actions:array<object{ label: string, variant: string, primary: boolean, onTap: Action }>, alignment:Alignment, backgroundColor:Color, clipBehavior:string, content:string | Widget, dismissible:boolean (default true), elevation:Dimension, insetPadding:EdgeInsets, onClose:Action, scrollable:boolean, shadowColor:Color, shape:object, surfaceTintColor:Color, title:string.

documents.title: align widget
documents.content:
`align` — layout, Core profile. Aligns a single child at a specified alignment.
Required: child:Widget.
Optional: alignment:Alignment (default center), heightFactor:number, widthFactor:number.

documents.title: animatedAlign widget
documents.content:
`animatedAlign` — animation, Core profile. Implicitly animates a child's `alignment` within its bounds. Use for slide-from-edge / settle-to-position micro-interactions.
Required: alignment:Alignment, child:Widget.
Optional: curve:AnimationCurve (default easeInOut), duration:Dimension (default 300), onEnd:Action.

documents.title: animatedContainer widget
documents.content:
`animatedContainer` — animation, Core profile. Container that implicitly animates property changes. Whenever any of the size/decoration/alignment/padding fields change between builds the runtime tweens between the old and new values over `duration` using `curve`.

documents.content:

documents.title: animatedOpacity widget

documents.content:

documents.content:
`breadcrumb` — navigation, Core profile. Trail of ancestor locations ending at the current one. Composable from `linear` + `text` + navigate actions, but composing it loses the landmark role assistive technology uses to skip to it, and every author re-decides where the separator goes and whether the last item is a link (it is not).

documents.content:

Do NOT use a property named `action` — the runtime ignores it. Properties: variant:'elevated'|'filled'|'outlined'|'text'|'icon' (default 'elevated'; those five are the whole set — 'tonal' is not one of them and is rejected), icon:IconRef, enabled:bool. onTap is canonical {type:'tool', tool:'<name>', params:{...}} (see actions doc). documents.title: combobox widget
documents.content:
`combobox` (also `autocomplete`) — input, Core profile. Text entry with suggestions. Shared rows per §2.6.0; `binding` holds the **typed string**, not an option id. The defining property is that a value outside `options` is legal — that is what separates it from `select` / `multiSelect`, where the option list is the domain. Composing it from `textInput` + a list loses focus ownership: the list must not steal focus from the field, arrow keys must move a highlight without moving the caret, and Escape must close the list without clearing the text. Those are one widget's job.
Optional: allowCustom:boolean (default true), debounceMs:number (default 250), label:string, minChars:number (default 1), onSearch:Action, options:array<Option> (alias items), placeholder:string.

documents.title: conditional widget
documents.content:
`conditional` — layout, Core profile. Renders different branches based on an expression. Two forms are supported: then/else and multi-branch (`switch`/`cases`).
Optional: cases:array, condition:boolean | binding, default:Widget, else:Widget, switch:binding, then:Widget (alias child/widget).

Notes: conditional renders one of two branches based on a boolean binding. Required: type:'conditional', condition:bool|string, then:<Widget>. Optional: else:<Widget>. condition evaluates via _isTruthy: null/false/0/empty-string/empty-list/empty-map are falsy. Note: equality expressions like {{a == b}} are NOT supported — use plain bindings to a precomputed boolean OR rely on truthy/falsy of values. Example: {"type":"conditional","condition":"{{loaded}}","then":{"type":"text","text":"ready"},"else":{"type":"text","text":"loading…"}}.

documents.title: contextMenu widget
documents.content:
`contextMenu` — interaction, Core profile. Menu raised by secondary activation on its `child` — right-click, long press, or the platform's context key. This cannot be composed: the gesture that raises it is platform-specific (and on touch competes with scroll and text selection), and the menu must appear at the pointer rather than against the child's box. A `gestureDetector` wrapping a `popupMenuButton` gets neither.
Required: child:Widget, items:array<object>.
Optional: enabled:boolean (default true).

documents.content:

documents.title: dateRangePicker widget
documents.content:
`dateRangePicker` — input, Core profile. Date range selection. Exception to §2.6.0: instead of a single `binding`, the range is bound via **two separate properties** — `startDate` and `endDate` — each independently following §2.6.0 two-way semantics (each accepts a literal ISO string, a `{{path}}` expression for read-only display, or a plain state-path string for two-way binding). `firstDate`/`lastDate` remain one-way constraints on the allowed range.

documents.content:
`dateTimePicker` — input, Core profile. Single instant — date and time chosen together. Shared rows per §2.6.0; `binding` holds one ISO-8601 timestamp. Not `datePicker` + `timePicker` side by side: those bind two values the author must then recombine, and the recombination is where time zones get lost. One widget, one instant, one binding.
Optional: dateFormat:string, label:string, max:string, min:string, minuteInterval:number (default 1), timeFormat:string, timeZone:string.

Read-only by design — editing a diff means editing one side, which is `codeEditor`'s job.

documents.title: fileInput widget
documents.content:
`fileInput` — input, Core profile. Lets the user hand the application a file they picked themselves. Follows the shared input contract (spec §2.6.0): with `binding` set, the runtime writes the selection to that state path. The value written is a list of file descriptors — see `binding` below. **Why this is Core and `client.selectFile` is not.** Reading a path the document names (`client.readFile`, `client.listFiles` — spec §8.2) reaches into the host's filesystem, so it belongs to the Client Profile behind a `file.read` grant (spec §8.4). Receiving a file the *user chose in a picker* is the opposite: the choosing is the consent, and the app learns nothing it was not handed. It is the same trust level as `signature` (also Core), which already accepts user-drawn input. A browser-rendered app that cannot claim the Client Profile still must be able to accept an upload. A runtime MUST NOT use this widget as a path to unpicked files: only what the picker returned is readable, and `path` MAY be absent (it is on web). Transport is not this widget's concern — once the selection is in state, sending it is an ordinary `tool` action.
Optional: accept:array<string>, aspectRatio:number, binding:string, crop:boolean (default false), dragDrop:boolean (default true), enabled:boolean (default true), label:string, maxBytes:number, maxFiles:number, multiple:boolean (default false), onChange:Action, onError:Action, preview:boolean (default false).

documents.title: gantt widget
documents.content:
`gantt` — advanced, Advanced profile. Tasks on a time axis, with dependencies and progress. What makes this a widget rather than a composition is the axis. Bars are positioned by *time*, not by index, so the row and the header must share one scale, stay aligned through zoom and horizontal scroll, and place a task whose span is shorter than a pixel without dropping it. Composing it from `grid` gives rows that drift from the header as soon as either scrolls. Dependencies are drawn, not enforced: the widget renders the arrows and reports an edit, and whether a move is legal is the server's answer.
Required: tasks:array<object> | binding.
Optional: editable:boolean (default false), range:object, rowHeight:number, showDependencies:boolean (default true), showProgress:boolean (default true), todayMarker:boolean (default true), viewMode:string (one of hour|day|week|month|quarter|year; default day).

documents.title: hero widget
documents.content:
`hero` — animation, Core profile. Shared-element transition wrapper. Wrap a child widget on the source page AND on the destination page with the SAME `tag`; the runtime morphs the source widget's bounds → destination widget's bounds during the route transition (cover → detail magnification, album cover → expanded album view). Pairs naturally with `RouteTransition` styles such as `fade` or `sharedAxis`.
Required: child:Widget, tag:string.
Optional: flightShuttleBuilder:Widget, transitionOnUserGestures:boolean (default false).

documents.title: icon widget
documents.content:
`icon` — display, Core profile. Displays an icon. The `icon` property accepts three source forms — pick the lightest option that fits the asset: 1. **Named (built-in)** — `"home"`, `"folder_open"`, … from the runtime's Material Icons resolver table. Zero-cost. 2. **Codepoint** — `{codepoint, fontFamily?, fontPackage?}` for Material Icons codepoints not in the name table. 3. **Any `AssetRef`** — a network URL, `bundle://` asset, `assets/` path, `data:image/svg+xml;…` inline SVG, `client://` host resource, or an `{uri, origin?}` object read from an origin. Which of these a given runtime resolves is declared, not assumed (`06_Runtime_Contract.md` §6.12). A bare string that matches no known scheme and is not an `assets/` path is read as a **name**, so the named form stays the zero-ceremony default. The optional `shader` field paints the icon with a gradient/shader fill (rather than a solid `color`). When both are set the shader wins.
Required: icon:IconRef.
Optional: color:Color, shader:Gradient, size:string|number, sizeToken:string (one of sm|md|lg|xl).

Notes: icon renders a Material icon. The property is `icon`, not `name` — the factory reads only `properties['icon']`, so `name` renders nothing. Required: type:'icon', icon:string (Material icon name like 'home', 'add', 'folder_open', 'settings'). Properties: size:number, color:string. Example: {"type":"icon","icon":"home","size":20,"color":"#7DD3FC"}. Common names: home, add, close, edit, delete, folder, folder_open, settings, info, warning, error, search, refresh, play_arrow, stop, chevron_left, chevron_right, expand_more, expand_less, more_vert, extension, star, push_pin, history.

documents.title: iconButton widget
documents.content:
`iconButton` — input, Core profile. Icon-only button for compact actions.
Required: icon:IconRef.
Optional: alignment:Alignment, color:Color, disabledColor:Color, enableFeedback:boolean, enabled:boolean (default true), fontFamily:string, highlightColor:Color, iconSize:Dimension, onTap:Action, padding:EdgeInsets, size:number, splashColor:Color, splashRadius:Dimension.

documents.title: image widget
documents.content:
`image` — display, Core profile. Displays an image from any asset source the runtime resolves — a network URL, the active bundle, inline bytes, a host resource, or a resource served by an origin. See `AssetRef`; a runtime declares which of those it resolves (`06_Runtime_Contract.md` §6.12) and routes the rest to `fallback` / `fallbackUrl` / `fallbackBehavior`.
Required: src:AssetRef (alias source/backgroundImage).
Optional: alignment:Alignment (default center), errorWidget:string, fallback:Widget, fallbackBehavior:string, fallbackUrl:AssetRef, fit:string (one of cover|contain|fill|none|scaleDown|fitHeight|fitWidth; default contain), height:number, loading:Widget, placeholder:string, width:number.

documents.title: imageFilter widget
documents.content:
`imageFilter` — display, Core profile. Wraps a child with a colour / blur filter. Distinct from `BoxDecoration.image.colorFilter` (which colours an image background) — `imageFilter` filters the entire rendered subtree. Use for sepia/grayscale book pages, blur-on-hover thumbnails, saturation-bumped hero shots.
Required: child:Widget, filter:string (one of sepia|grayscale|blur|saturation|brightness|contrast|invert).
Optional: intensity:number (default 1.0).

documents.content:

Optional: alignment:Alignment (default topStart), clipBehavior:string, index:number | binding (default 0), sizing:string, textDirection:string.

documents.content:

Optional: autofocus:boolean, borderRadius:number, canRequestFocus:boolean, customBorder:object, enableFeedback:boolean, excludeFromSemantics:boolean, focusColor:Color, highlightColor:Color, hoverColor:Color, onDoubleTap:Action, onHighlightChanged:Action, onHover:Action, onLongPress:Action, onTap:Action, onTapCancel:Action, onTapDown:Action, onTapUp:Action, overlayColor:Color, splashColor:Color, splashRadius:Dimension.

documents.content:
`intrinsicHeight` — layout, Core profile. Constrains a child to the intrinsic height required by its content.

documents.title: intrinsicWidth widget
documents.content:

documents.title: kanban widget
documents.content:
`kanban` — advanced, Advanced profile. Cards in columns, moved between columns by dragging. Composable from `grid` + `draggable` + `dragTarget` in the sense that the pieces exist — and that composition is where the work actually is. Drop targets must be the gaps between cards rather than the cards themselves, the column must auto-scroll while a card hovers near its edge, and a drop must report *where* in the destination the card landed, not just that it moved. Authors composing this get a board that looks right and reorders wrongly. The widget owns presentation and gesture. It does **not** own the move: `onCardMove` reports the intent and the author's action decides, so a server-rejected move is not silently already applied on screen.
Required: columns:array<object> | binding, itemTemplate:Widget.
Optional: columnWidth:Dimension, draggable:boolean (default true), itemKey:string (default id), optimistic:boolean (default false).

documents.title: kenBurnsImage widget
documents.content:
`kenBurnsImage` — display, Core profile. Image with an automatic slow zoom-and-pan animation (the "Ken Burns effect"). Used for cinematic stills in book chapter openings, landing pages, and slideshow frames. The image holds intrinsic resolution and is animated within fit-bounds — no cropping outside the rendered rectangle.
Required: src:AssetRef.
Optional: curve:AnimationCurve (default linear), duration:Dimension (default 8000), endAlignment:Alignment (default bottomEnd), fit:string (one of cover|contain|fill|fitWidth|fitHeight; default cover), height:Dimension, intensity:number (default 0.15), loop:boolean (default true), startAlignment:Alignment (default topStart), width:Dimension.

documents.title: layoutBuilder widget
documents.content:
`layoutBuilder` — utility, Core profile. Runtime-only responsive container: picks a child by matching the current constraints against a breakpoint map.
Optional: breakpoints:object, default:Widget, layouts:object.

documents.title: lazy widget
documents.content:
`lazy` — utility, Core profile. Defer rendering of an expensive subtree until it enters the viewport (or until explicitly loaded).
Optional: child:Widget, children:array<Widget>, content:Widget | object (alias child), delay:number, onError:Action, onLoad:Action, placeholder:Widget, trigger:string (one of visible|immediate|manual; default visible).

documents.title: lightbox widget
documents.content:
`lightbox` — advanced, Core profile. Full-screen modal image viewer with pinch-zoom and swipe-between- images. Used as a tap target on a thumbnail image — opening the lightbox transitions the thumbnail into the full-screen view. Pairs naturally with `hero` for the cover-to-detail morph.
Required: images:array<AssetRef>.
Optional: allowSwipe:boolean (default true), allowZoom:boolean (default true), backgroundColor:Color (default #FF000000), initialIndex:number (default 0), maxZoom:number (default 4.0), onClose:Action, onIndexChanged:Action.

documents.title: limitedBox widget
documents.content:
`limitedBox` — utility, Core profile. Limits a child's size only when it would otherwise be unbounded.
Required: child:Widget.
Optional: maxHeight:number (default double.infinity), maxWidth:number (default double.infinity).

documents.title: linear widget
documents.content:
`linear` (also `row`, `column`) — layout, Core profile. Linear (flex) layout along a single axis. Replaces separate `row` / `column` widgets — use `direction: "horizontal"` or `direction: "vertical"`. Main-axis sizing: when at least one child is `expanded` / `flexible` / `spacer` (or carries a `flex` value), `linear` expands to fill the available main-axis space so those children can distribute the remainder; otherwise it shrink-wraps its children. Authors can override this with the explicit `mainAxisSize` property.
Required: children:array<Widget>, direction:string (default vertical; alias orientation/scrollDirection).
Optional: alignment:string (one of start|center|end|stretch; default start; alias crossAxisAlignment), distribution:string (one of start|center|end|spaceBetween|spaceAround|spaceEvenly; default start; alias mainAxisAlignment), mainAxisSize:string (one of min|max), padding:EdgeInsets, spacing:number (default 0; alias gap/itemSpacing), wrap:boolean.

Notes: linear is the row/column layout widget. Replaces Flutter's Row/Column. Required: type:'linear', children:[<Widget>...]. Properties: direction:'horizontal'|'vertical' (default horizontal), gap:number (spacing between children), mainAxisAlignment:'start'|'center'|'end'|'spaceBetween'|'spaceAround'|'spaceEvenly', crossAxisAlignment:'start'|'center'|'end'|'stretch', mainAxisSize:'min'|'max'. Example vertical: {"type":"linear","direction":"vertical","gap":8,"children":[{"type":"text","text":"a"},{"type":"text","text":"b"}]}.

documents.title: link widget
documents.content:
`link` (also `navLink`) — navigation, Core profile. Text that navigates. `route` goes to an internal route; `url` leaves the application through `navigation.openUrl` (§4.3.3). Exactly one of the two is set — a link that could mean either is a link whose destination the author did not decide. Composable from `inkWell` + `text` + an action, and the composition is what most documents do today. It loses the link role (assistive technology announces "button"), the visited/hover affordances, and — for `url` — the external-destination cue a user needs before leaving the app. `navLink` is the same widget with `activeWhen` in use: a link that knows whether it points at where you already are.
Required: label:string.
Optional: activeWhen:string | binding, child:Widget, icon:IconRef, params:object, route:string, target:string (one of new|same; default new), underline:string (one of always|hover|never; default hover), url:string.

documents.title: list widget
documents.content:
`list` (also `listView`, `listview`) — list, Core profile. Scrollable linear collection rendered from an array binding.
Optional: children:array<Widget>, emptyMessage:string, itemBuilder:Widget, itemCount:number, itemExtent:number, itemHeight:number, itemTemplate:Widget, items:array | binding, orientation:string (default vertical), overscan:number (default 3), padding:EdgeInsets, physics:string, reverse:boolean, scrollCacheExtent:Dimension, scrollDirection:string, shrinkWrap:boolean, spacing:number (default 0), template:object|string, virtual:boolean (default false).

Notes: list renders a collection. Required: type:'list', either children:[<Widget>...] OR items:array + itemTemplate:<Widget>. With itemTemplate, each row is rendered from the template with {{item}} and {{index}} bound to the current entry. Properties: orientation:'vertical'|'horizontal' (default vertical), spacing:number, emptyMessage:string, itemExtent:number, shrinkWrap:bool and padding:number|EdgeInsets are read by the runtime but not declared in 1.4 — they work at run time and the conformance check rejects them, so prefer a surrounding box for padding. Use itemTemplate over children for bound dynamic lists. Example: {"type":"list","items":"{{todos}}","shrinkWrap":true,"itemTemplate":{"type":"linear","children":[{"type":"text","text":"{{item.title}}"}]}}.

documents.content:

documents.content:

`map` — advanced, Core profile. Geographic map with markers and overlays.

documents.content:
`mediaPlayer` (also `video`, `audio`) — advanced, Core profile. Audio / video player widget.

documents.title: mediaQuery widget
documents.content:
`mediaQuery` — utility, Core profile. Responsive widget that inspects the current layout context and picks a child based on media-query conditions. Supports a `then`/`else` expression form and a `breakpoints` map form. The binding engine exposes `{{media.width}}`, `{{media.height}}`, `{{media.orientation}}` inside `condition`.
Optional: breakpoints:object, condition:object | binding, defaultChild:Widget, else:Widget, then:Widget.

documents.title: menu widget
documents.content:
`menu` — navigation, Core profile. Standing list of navigation destinations, optionally nested. Unlike `popupMenuButton` (a trigger that opens a transient list) this one is part of the layout — a sidebar or an inline section list. `navigationRail` covers the icon-rail form on one axis with a flat item set; this covers nesting, collapsing, and the expanded/collapsed sidebar that admin screens are built from.
Required: items:array<object>.
Optional: collapsed:boolean | binding, mode:string (one of vertical|horizontal|inline; default vertical), openKeys:array<string>, selectedKey:string | binding.

documents.title: multiSelect widget
documents.content:
`multiSelect` — input, Core profile. Dropdown selection of more than one value. Shared rows per §2.6.0; `binding` holds an **array** of selected values. Distinct from `checkboxGroup`, which lays every option out at once: this keeps the closed/summary form of `select` and is what a long option list needs. Distinct from `select`, which is single-value — the two are kept apart rather than folded into a `multiple` flag because the bound value changes shape (scalar vs array), and a flag that silently changes the type of what lands in state is the kind of thing an author discovers at runtime.
Required: options:array<Option> (alias items).
Optional: label:string, maxSelections:number, placeholder:string, searchable:boolean (default false), selectAll:boolean (default false), showChips:boolean (default true).

documents.title: navigationRail widget
documents.content:
`navigationRail` — navigation, Core profile. Vertical navigation rail for tablet/desktop layouts. Each item's text field is `label`.
Required: items:array<NavItem> (alias destinations).
Optional: backgroundColor:Color, change:Action, elevation:Dimension, extended:boolean, groupAlignment:number, labelType:string, leading:Widget, minExtendedWidth:Dimension, minWidth:Dimension, onChange:Action, onSelect:Action, selectedIconTheme:object, selectedIndex:number | binding, selectedLabelTextStyle:TextStyle, trailing:Widget, unselectedIconTheme:object, unselectedLabelTextStyle:TextStyle.

documents.content:
`networkGraph` — advanced, Core profile. Network topology graph. Same node/edge model as `graph`, with topology-oriented defaults (hierarchical layout, directed edges).
Optional: edgeColor:Color, edges:array<object>, height:Dimension, interactive:boolean, labelColor:Color, layout:string, nodeColor:Color, nodes:array<object>, onEdgeTap:Action, onNodeTap:Action, width:Dimension.

documents.title: numberField widget
documents.content:
`numberField` (also `numberInput`) — input, Core profile. Specialized input for numeric values. Shared rows per §2.6.0; `value` is `number`.
Optional: change:Action, decimalPlaces:number (default 0), error:string, format:string, helperText:string, hint:string, label:string, max:number, min:number, prefix:string, showStepper:boolean (default true), step:number (default 1), suffix:string, thousandSeparator:boolean|string.

documents.title: numberStepper widget
documents.content:
`numberStepper` — input, Core profile. Incremental numeric input with plus/minus buttons. Shared rows per §2.6.0; `value` is `number`.
Optional: change:Action, color:Color, label:string, max:number, min:number, size:string (one of small|medium|large), step:number (default 1).

documents.title: offlineFallback widget
documents.content:
`offlineFallback` — utility, Core profile. Swaps between an online widget and an offline fallback based on connectivity tracked by the runtime. Connectivity state may be pinned by an `isOnline` binding for tests.
Optional: icon:IconRef, isOnline:boolean | binding, message:string, offline:Widget, onRetry:Action, online:Widget, showRetry:boolean (default true).

documents.title: opacity widget
documents.content:
`opacity` — animation, Core profile. Wraps a child with opacity, with optional animation.
Required: child:Widget, opacity:number | binding.
Optional: animated:boolean (default false), curve:string (default easeInOut), duration:number (default 300).

documents.title: otpInput widget
documents.content:
`otpInput` — input, Core profile. Fixed-length one-time-code entry. Shared rows per §2.6.0; `binding` holds the concatenated string, not per-cell values. This exists because the composed version is reliably broken. A row of `textInput`s loses: pasting a full code (it lands entirely in the first cell), forward focus movement on entry and backward on delete, and the platform's one-time-code autofill, which needs a single field declaring that intent. None of the three can be recovered by the author.
Optional: autofill:boolean (default true), inputType:string (one of numeric|alphanumeric; default numeric), length:number (default 6), masked:boolean (default false), onComplete:Action.

documents.title: padding widget
documents.content:
`padding` — layout, Core profile. Applies padding around a single child.
Required: child:Widget, padding:EdgeInsets.

documents.title: pageView widget
documents.content:
`pageView` — scroll, Core profile. Full-viewport paged scroll view. Snaps one page per swipe; ideal for book pages, photo galleries, onboarding flows. Distinct from `carousel` (partial-viewport, peeking neighbours) — pageView is always one full page. Each child is rendered as a separate page.
Required: children:array<Widget>.
Optional: allowImplicitScrolling:boolean (default false), clipBehavior:string, direction:string (one of horizontal|vertical; default horizontal), initialPage:number (default 0), loop:boolean (default false), onChange:Action, onPageChanged:Action, padEnds:boolean, pageSnapping:boolean, reverse:boolean, scrollDirection:string, scrollPhysics:string (one of bouncing|clamping|neverScrollable; default clamping).

documents.title: pagination widget
documents.content:
`pagination` — navigation, Core profile. Page selector for a paged collection. `binding` holds the current page (1-based). The composed version is where off-by-one bugs live: first/last bounds, the ellipsis window, and disabling prev/next at the ends are re-derived by every author. Stating it once also fixes what a screen reader hears — "page 3 of 12", not "3".
Required: total:number.
Optional: binding:string, current:number, pageSize:number (default 20), pageSizeOptions:array<number>, showSizeChanger:boolean (default false), showTotal:boolean (default false), siblingCount:number (default 1).

documents.title: pdfViewer widget
documents.content:
`pdfViewer` — advanced, Advanced profile. Renders a PDF document with page navigation and zoom. `webView` can display a PDF where the host has a plugin for it, and that is the substitution to avoid: the document then belongs to the browser, so page position, zoom, and search are outside the DSL's reach and outside the app's theme. A viewer widget keeps them addressable. `src` is an `AssetRef`, so the same document works from a bundle, a URL, a picked file (`fileInput` writes a `data:` URI), or a server resource.
Required: src:AssetRef.
Optional: fit:string (one of width|height|page; default width), height:Dimension, page:number | binding, showPageNav:boolean (default true), showToolbar:boolean (default true), showZoom:boolean (default true), zoom:number | binding.

documents.title: permissionPrompt widget
documents.content:
`permissionPrompt` — utility, Core profile. Presents a prompt for one or more client capabilities (e.g., clipboard, filesystem). See [`07_Security.md`](07_Security.md) for the permission vocabulary.
Optional: allowPartial:boolean (default false), description:string, icon:IconRef, onAllow:Action, onDeny:Action, permissionType:string, permissions:array<string>, style:string (one of inline|dialog|banner; default inline), title:string.

documents.title: placeholder widget
documents.content:
`placeholder` (also `skeleton`) — display, Core profile. Empty placeholder widget with optional dimensions and color.
Optional: child:Widget, color:Color, fallbackHeight:number, fallbackWidth:number, strokeWidth:number.

documents.title: popover widget
documents.content:
`popover` (also `hoverCard`) — dialog, Core profile. Transient surface anchored to a trigger. `child` is the trigger; `content` is what appears. Distinct from `tooltip` (text only, no focusable content) and from `customDialog` (modal, centred, takes the whole screen's attention). A popover keeps the page usable behind it and is positioned against its anchor, which is the part composition cannot supply: flipping to the other side when it would overflow the viewport, and returning focus to the trigger on dismiss. `hoverCard` is the same widget with `trigger: "hover"`.
Required: child:Widget, content:Widget.
Optional: closeDelay:number (default 0), dismissOnOutside:boolean (default true), open:boolean | binding, openDelay:number (default 0), placement:string (one of top|bottom|start|end|auto; default auto), trigger:string (one of tap|hover|focus|manual; default tap).

documents.title: popupMenuButton widget
documents.content:
`popupMenuButton` (also `dropdownMenu`) — navigation, Core profile. Button that reveals a popup menu of options.
Required: items:array<MenuItem>.
Optional: change:Action, color:Color, elevation:Dimension, icon:IconRef (default more_vert), iconSize:Dimension, offset:object, onCanceled:Action, onChange:Action, onOpened:Action, onSelect:Action, padding:EdgeInsets, shadowColor:Color, shape:object, splashRadius:Dimension, surfaceTintColor:Color.

documents.content:

Required: child:Widget.
Optional: bottom:Dimension, height:Dimension, left:Dimension, right:Dimension, top:Dimension, width:Dimension.

documents.title: progressBar widget
documents.content:
`progressBar` (also `linearProgressIndicator`, `loadingIndicator`, `loading-indicator`, `progress-bar`, `progress`) — display, Core profile. Progress indicator (linear or circular).
Optional: backgroundColor:Color, color:Color (default theme primary), indicatorType:string (default linear), size:Dimension, strokeWidth:Dimension, value:number | binding.

documents.title: qrCode widget
documents.content:
`qrCode` — advanced, Advanced profile. Renders a QR code for `value`. Cannot be composed — the module grid is computed, not laid out. The definition is small in exchange, and it pairs with the scanning side the platform already has: a code produced here is the same artefact §8.9 reads on arrival.
Required: value:string | binding.
Optional: backgroundColor:Color, errorCorrection:string (one of low|medium|quartile|high; default M), foregroundColor:Color, logo:AssetRef, margin:boolean (default true), size:number (default 200).

documents.title: radio widget
documents.content:
`radio` — input, Core profile. Single radio button. The group's selected value is bound via `groupValue` (or the enclosing `radioGroup`'s `binding`).
Required: groupValue:any | binding, value:any.
Optional: activeColor:Color, binding:string, change:Action, fillColor:Color, focusColor:Color, hoverColor:Color, label:string, onChange:Action, splashRadius:Dimension.

documents.title: radioGroup widget
documents.content:
`radioGroup` — input, Core profile. Single-selection radio group. Shared rows per §2.6.0.
Required: options:array<Option> (alias items).
Optional: direction:string, label:string, orientation:string (default vertical).

documents.title: rangeSlider widget
documents.content:
`rangeSlider` — input, Core profile. Range selection with two thumbs. Shared rows per §2.6.0; `value` is an object `{ start, end }`.
Optional: activeColor:Color, change:Action, divisions:number, inactiveColor:Color, labels:array<string>, max:number (default 1), min:number (default 0), onChangeEnd:Action, onChangeStart:Action.

documents.title: rating widget
documents.content:
`rating` — input, Core profile. Discrete rating control (e.g., star rating). Shared rows per §2.6.0; `value` is `number`.
Optional: allowHalf:boolean, change:Action, color:Color, emptyColor:Color, icon:IconRef (default star), max:number (default 5), readOnly:boolean, size:Dimension.

documents.title: resizable widget
documents.content:
`resizable` — layout, Advanced profile. A box the user can resize by dragging its edges or corners. Distinct from `splitter`, which divides a fixed area between siblings. This changes one widget's own size against whatever surrounds it.
Required: child:Widget.
Optional: handles:array<string>, height:number | binding, keepAspectRatio:boolean (default false), maxHeight:number, maxWidth:number, minHeight:number, minWidth:number, width:number | binding.

documents.title: richText widget
documents.content:
`richText` — display, Core profile. Multi-span styled text — paragraph composition for long-form content (articles, book chapters, captions with inline emphasis or icons). Each `Span` is either a styled text run or an inline widget; the paragraph-level `style` provides the base TextStyle that individual span styles layer on top of.
Required: spans:array<Span>.
Optional: dropCap:DropCap, maxLines:number, overflow:string (one of clip|ellipsis|fade|visible; default clip), softWrap:boolean (default true), style:TextStyle, textAlign:string (one of start|end|left|right|center|justify; default start), textDirection:string (one of ltr|rtl), textScaleFactor:number.

documents.title: richTextEditor widget
documents.content:
`richTextEditor` — advanced, Advanced profile. Formatted text entry. Shared rows per §2.6.0. **The bound value is HTML**, a subset stated in `format` below. That choice is the whole reason this widget needed a decision rather than a definition: an editor's value format is a contract every consumer of the document inherits, and a proprietary delta model would make the content unreadable to anything but the editor that produced it. HTML is what `richText` and `markdown` already sit beside, and a host that cannot edit can still display it. A runtime MUST sanitise on the way in and on the way out — §7.5 applies to this value exactly as it applies to any other author-supplied markup. The editor is not a licence to inject.
Optional: binding:string, format:string (one of html|markdown; default html), maxLength:number, minHeight:number, onChange:Action, placeholder:string, toolbar:array<string>.

documents.title: rive widget
documents.content:
`rive` — animation, Core profile. Plays a Rive animation (`.riv` asset) — the alternative to `lottieAnimation` when the asset was authored in Rive. State-machine inputs are driven via `inputs` so the same asset reacts to host state changes (toggle, scrub, trigger). Distinct from Lottie: Rive supports interactive state machines, vector deformation, and smaller binary footprints; Lottie is After Effects-based and better suited to time-driven motion graphics.
Required: src:AssetRef.
Optional: alignment:Alignment (default center), animation:string, artboard:string, fit:string (one of fill|contain|cover|fitWidth|fitHeight|none|scaleDown; default contain), height:Dimension, inputs:object, stateMachine:string, width:Dimension.

documents.title: safeArea widget
documents.content:
`safeArea` — layout, Core profile. Insets children so they avoid system UI overlaps (notch, status bar, home indicator).
Required: child:Widget.
Optional: bottom:boolean, left:boolean, maintainBottomViewPadding:boolean, minimum:EdgeInsets, right:boolean, top:boolean.

documents.title: scrollAnimated widget
documents.content:
`scrollAnimated` — animation, Core profile. Animation driven by scroll position rather than time. Wraps a child and reads from an ancestor scroll view's offset. Each `binding` maps a scroll-offset window to a property tween — when scroll passes through `[fromOffset, toOffset]` the property interpolates between `fromValue` and `toValue` linearly (or via `curve`). Common uses: parallax masthead (image translates 50% scroll speed), reveal-on-scroll (fade in as element enters viewport), shrinking title (font scales as user scrolls down).
Required: bindings:array<object>, child:Widget.

documents.title: scrollBar widget
documents.content:
`scrollBar` — scroll, Core profile. Wraps a scrollable child with a visible scroll bar. The runtime MUST provide a shared scroll controller to both the scroll bar and its scrollable child. When `thumbVisibility` or `trackVisibility` is `true`, the controller is required to drive the visibility; omitting it is a runtime error. Authors SHOULD NOT manage the controller manually — the runtime injects it transparently so the child scrollable (`scrollView`, `singleChildScrollView`, `list`, `grid`, `pageView`) binds to the same position.
Optional: child:Widget, children:array<Widget>, radius:number, thickness:number, thumbVisibility:boolean, trackVisibility:boolean.

documents.title: scrollView widget
documents.content:
`scrollView` (also `scrollArea`) — scroll, Core profile. Scrollable viewport. Two layout modes — pick one per instance: - **Linear mode** — `child` (single widget) or `children` (wrapped in an implicit linear column along `direction`). Simplest for everyday scrolling content. - **Sliver mode** — `slivers` array of `Sliver` primitives. Use for collapsing app bars, sticky section headers, parallax mastheads, or mixing list/grid sections in one viewport. The three input slots (`child`, `children`, `slivers`) are mutually exclusive.
Optional: child:Widget, children:array<Widget>, direction:string (one of vertical|horizontal; default vertical), padding:EdgeInsets, primary:boolean, reverse:boolean, scrollDirection:string, scrollPhysics:string (one of bouncing|clamping|neverScrollable; default clamping), slivers:array<Sliver>.

documents.content:
`splitter` — layout, Advanced profile. Panes separated by draggable gutters. Distinct from `resizable`, which resizes one box against the layout around it. This divides a fixed area between siblings: dragging a gutter takes space from one pane and gives it to the next, so the total never changes.

Optional: collapsible:array<boolean>, gutterSize:number (default 8), minSizes:array<number>, orientation:string (one of horizontal|vertical; default horizontal), sizes:array<number> | binding.

documents.title: spreadsheet widget
documents.content:
`spreadsheet` — advanced, Advanced profile. Editable grid of cells addressed by row and column, with optional formulas. Distinct from `dataTable`, which presents records: a table's unit is a row with typed fields, a spreadsheet's unit is a cell with a coordinate. That difference is why one cannot be a mode of the other — selection, editing, and paste all address different things. **Formulas are evaluated by the runtime's expression engine under §7.1**, not by a spreadsheet language of the DSL's own. A runtime that cannot meet that sandbox MUST render formulas as their last computed value rather than evaluating them loosely: a cell that runs arbitrary text is the one place this widget could become an injection surface.
Required: data:array<array> | binding.
Optional: columnHeaders:boolean (default true), columns:array<object>, editable:boolean (default true), formulas:boolean (default false), frozenColumns:number (default 0), frozenRows:number (default 0), rowHeaders:boolean (default true).

documents.content:
`staggeredGrid` — list, Core profile. Pinterest-style masonry layout — items keep their intrinsic height and are packed by column without uniform row alignment. Use for album / book / portfolio shelves where covers have different aspect ratios. Distinct from `grid` (uniform row alignment) and `carousel` (single-axis scrolling).
Required: columns:number | object.
Optional: children:array<Widget>, crossAxisSpacing:number (default 0), itemTemplate:Widget, items:array | binding, mainAxisSpacing:number (default 0), padding:EdgeInsets, scrollDirection:string (one of vertical|horizontal; default vertical).

documents.content:

Example: {"type":"text","text":"Hello {{name}}","variant":"titleMedium","style":{"color":"#7DD3FC"}}.

documents.title: view widget
documents.content:
`view` — utility, Composition profile. Embeds a definition sourced from anywhere — including another MCP origin — at this point in the tree. The consumer side of composition: `11_Bundle_Metadata.md` §11.9 `dashboard` declares how an app presents itself *when embedded*; `view` is how an app *embeds*. See [`01_Core_Concepts.md`](01_Core_Concepts.md) §1.9 for `DefinitionSource` and the origin-scope rule. When `source` names an origin, that origin becomes the ambient origin for the embedded subtree: its `tool` calls, resource reads, subscriptions, state, storage, and permissions all scope to it (§1.9.5, §7.10, §8.8). This is what lets a definition authored with no knowledge of any embedder render unmodified and still reach its own server.
Required: source:DefinitionSource.
Optional: fallback:Widget, loading:Widget, onError:Action, props:object, theme:string (one of inherit|own; default inherit).

documents.content:

documents.title: voiceInput widget
documents.content:
`voiceInput` — input, Client profile. Speech captured from the microphone, transcribed into `binding`. **Client Profile, not Core** — and the line is worth stating because `fileInput` sits on the other side of it. Picking a file is one act of choosing, and the choosing is the consent. A microphone is a continuous capture of the room, including whoever else is in it, so it belongs behind the permission system (§8.4) with a grant the user can see and revoke. There is no composition that reaches it: microphone access is a host capability, so without this widget a document cannot express the intent at all.
Optional: binding:string, continuous:boolean (default false), interimResults:boolean (default false), language:string, maxDuration:number, showWaveform:boolean (default true).

documents.title: state.initial — page state
documents.content: Every page can declare an initial state map under state.initial. NOT state directly — the wrap layer is state.initial:{}. The map's keys are addressable from any widget via {{key}} bindings. After initialize, the runtime owns the state tree; tool action results are auto-merged into top-level state (every key in the tool's outputSchema becomes a state key). Example: {"type":"page","state":{"initial":{"count":0,"text":""}},"content":...}. Anti-pattern: 'state':{...} directly (NOT supported).

documents.title: template bindings — {{path}}
documents.content: Any string value in a widget property can be a template binding using {{path}} syntax. The path is dot-separated for nested objects ({{user.name}}). For list items, the runtime injects {{item}} and {{index}} into the template scope. Bindings re-evaluate whenever the bound state changes — the widget rebuilds. Note: arithmetic and equality expressions ({{a + b}}, {{x == y}}) are NOT supported in this runtime version — pre-compute the value in tool handlers or use conditional with a precomputed boolean. Example simple value: 'value':'{{count}}'. Example list item: 'value':'{{item.title}}'.

documents.title: tool action — invoke an MCP tool
documents.content: Canonical action shape: {"type":"tool","tool":"<short.name>","params":{...}}. Anti-patterns: {action:'tool', args:{...}} (wrong field names — use type+params). Action params can include {{binding}} references — they're resolved at dispatch time. Tool responses are JSON-decoded and the top-level keys auto-merge into the page state (spec §3.10), so a tool returning {shouted:'HI'} sets state.shouted='HI' which downstream widgets like {"value":"{{shouted}}"} render automatically. Example button action: {"type":"button","label":"Run","onTap":{"type":"tool","tool":"shout","params":{"text":"{{input}}"}}}. The handler attaches under `click` (or its alias `onTap`) — NOT `action`; the runtime ignores `action`.

documents.title: callback event values — $event
documents.content: Custom widgets that fire callbacks with a value (onSelect getting a tab index, onChanged getting a text value, onPick getting a selected item) inject the value into action.params under the key $event. Authors can wire this through params.$event or reference it from within params for forwarding. Example: a list pick handler that records the picked index — {"onSelect":{"type":"tool","tool":"recordTab","params":{"index":"{{$event}}"}}}. The runtime resolves $event before dispatching the tool.

documents.title: lifecycle.onInit — auto-load on mount
documents.content: page.lifecycle.onInit fires ONCE after the runtime initializes the page tree. Common use: auto-call a refresh tool that populates initial state. Example: {"type":"page","lifecycle":{"onInit":{"type":"tool","tool":"refresh","params":{}}},"content":...}. Caveat in this runtime version: onInit may fire during initialize() before tool executors are registered — hosts re-fire onInit manually after registerToolExecutor. Authors do not need to handle this; just declare onInit and the host re-fires.

documents.title: tool response auto-merge — spec §3.10
documents.content: Every tool response (the JSON-decoded body) has its top-level keys auto-merged into the page state. Naming the output schema fields the same as the binding keys in widgets means zero glue code — tool returns {count:5} and widgets binding {{count}} update. Anti-pattern: declaring an explicit onSuccess on the action — that overrides the auto-merge and you must do the merge yourself. Just rely on auto-merge unless you need a custom side effect.
